question: To qualify to sit for the Georgia broker exam, an applicant must have held an active real estate license for what minimum period?
choice_a: At least 3 years within the previous 5 years
choice_b: At least 1 year within the previous 2 years
choice_c: At least 5 consecutive years immediately before applying
choice_d: At least 2 years within the previous 10 years
explanation: The current GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin states that all broker applicants must have held an active real estate license for a minimum of three years, within the previous five years, to qualify for the broker exam. Out-of-state experience is allowed if certified by that jurisdiction's licensing authority with certification less than one year old.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, broker exam eligibility

question: Which of the following satisfies Georgia's broker education prerequisite for exam eligibility?
choice_a: Completing a 25-hour Community Association Manager prelicense course
choice_b: Completing the 60-hour Broker's Prelicense Course at a GREC-approved school
choice_c: Completing only the 75-hour Salesperson Prelicense Course, with no further coursework
choice_d: Completing a single 6-hour license-law continuing education seminar
explanation: One accepted route to broker exam eligibility is completing the 60-hour Broker's Prelicense Course at a GREC-approved school. This is distinct from the 25-hour CAM prelicense course and the 75-hour salesperson course, neither of which alone satisfies the broker education requirement.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, broker education requirements

question: Besides the 60-hour Broker's Prelicense Course, which alternate college-coursework route also satisfies Georgia's broker education prerequisite?
choice_a: Any 15 quarter-hours of coursework in any subject from an accredited college
choice_b: A bachelor's degree in any field, regardless of coursework content
choice_c: 15 quarter-hours (or 9 semester-hours) of qualifying real-estate/law coursework from an accredited U.S. or Canadian college or law school, shown by official transcript
choice_d: 9 quarter-hours of general business coursework from an unaccredited school
explanation: Georgia accepts 15 quarter-hours (9 semester-hours) of qualifying real-estate/law coursework from an accredited U.S. or Canadian college or law school, supported by an official transcript, as an alternative to the 60-hour Broker's Prelicense Course.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, broker education requirements

question: An applicant completed 60 hours of prelicense coursework approved by another U.S. state's real estate regulator. Does this satisfy Georgia's broker education prerequisite?
choice_a: No -- only coursework taken at a GREC-approved Georgia school counts, regardless of hours
choice_b: No -- out-of-state coursework can only be used to satisfy the salesperson prelicense requirement, never the broker requirement
choice_c: Yes, but only if the applicant also retakes 30 of those hours at a Georgia school
choice_d: Yes -- 60 hours of prelicense coursework approved by another U.S. state's or a Canadian province's real estate regulator is an accepted alternate route
explanation: Georgia recognizes 60 hours of prelicense coursework approved by another U.S. state's or Canadian province's real estate regulator as a third accepted route to satisfying the broker education prerequisite, alongside the 60-hour Georgia Broker's Prelicense Course and the college-coursework route.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, broker education requirements

question: A licensed Community Association Manager (CAM) in Georgia wants to become a real estate broker. What additional education must the CAM complete?
choice_a: Either the 75-hour Salesperson Prelicense course, or 10 additional quarter-hours (6 additional semester-hours) of qualifying college coursework
choice_b: Nothing further -- the CAM license and its coursework automatically satisfy all broker prelicense education requirements
choice_c: Only a 5-hour CAM-to-broker bridge course offered exclusively by GREC
choice_d: The 60-hour Broker's Prelicense Course is waived entirely for any CAM applicant
explanation: A licensed CAM applying for a broker license must also complete either the 75-hour Salesperson Prelicense course or 10 additional quarter-hours (6 additional semester-hours) of qualifying college coursework -- the CAM's own 25-hour prelicense course does not by itself satisfy broker education requirements.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, CAM-to-broker education requirements

question: How does Georgia's Community Association Manager (CAM) license relate to the broker license?
choice_a: CAM is simply an entry-level tier of the broker license that automatically upgrades after 3 years
choice_b: CAM is a separate, distinct GREC license with its own exam, its own 25-hour prelicense course, and its own application track -- it does not substitute for or count toward broker qualification
choice_c: Passing the CAM exam automatically satisfies the broker exam requirement
choice_d: CAM licensees are legally brokers who merely specialize in community associations
explanation: CAM is a separate, distinct GREC license track -- with its own 48-item exam (14 Laws/Rules + 34 Practice items), its own 25-hour CAM Prelicense Course, and its own application process. It is not a broker license tier and does not substitute for broker qualification.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, CAM license track

question: A broker applicant who is immediately affiliating with a sponsoring firm submits a signed 'Sponsoring Broker Statement' naming that firm. What license status can this applicant receive directly at the PSI test center?
choice_a: An Inactive license that must later be activated by filing a separate 'Open A Firm' application
choice_b: A temporary 90-day provisional license pending GREC board review
choice_c: An Active license, issued as an Associate Broker affiliated with that firm
choice_d: No license may be issued at the test center; all broker licenses require a mailed paper application
explanation: An applicant who affiliates with a sponsoring firm and submits a signed Sponsoring Broker Statement naming that firm can receive an Active license directly at the PSI test center, functioning as an Associate Broker under that firm.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, license issuance at test center

question: A broker applicant who is not immediately affiliating with any firm passes the exam. What happens next in Georgia's licensing process?
choice_a: The applicant is automatically issued an Active independent broker license on the spot, with no further filings
choice_b: The applicant's exam results are voided and the applicant must retake the exam once a firm is identified
choice_c: The applicant must wait 3 years before any license can be issued in Georgia
choice_d: The applicant receives an Inactive license at the test center, then separately files either an 'Open A Firm' application (to start their own firm) or a 'Change of Qualifying Broker' application (to head an existing firm) with GREC
explanation: A broker applicant not immediately affiliating with a firm receives an Inactive license at the PSI test center, and then must separately file either an 'Open A Firm' application (to start a new firm) or a 'Change of Qualifying Broker' application (to head an existing firm) with GREC.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, license issuance at test center

question: In Georgia real estate practice, what does the term 'Qualifying Broker' refer to?
choice_a: The GREC-recognized broker designated as responsible for a particular firm
choice_b: A broker who has passed the exam but has not yet activated any license
choice_c: A junior broker still completing continuing education requirements
choice_d: A broker licensed in another state who has not yet qualified for reciprocity in Georgia
explanation: 'Qualifying Broker' is a real, GREC-recognized term for the broker who is designated as responsible for a Firm -- distinct from an Associate Broker, who instead affiliates with and works under a sponsoring firm's qualifying broker.

question: What criminal history documentation must a Georgia broker applicant submit with their application, and how current must it be?
choice_a: A notarized personal statement swearing the applicant has no criminal history, with no report required
choice_b: A certified criminal history report from the Georgia Crime Information Center (GCIC), or an equivalent report from the applicant's state of residency if not a Georgia resident, no more than 60 days old
choice_c: A GCIC report that may be any age, as long as it predates the application by less than 5 years
choice_d: An FBI fingerprint clearance letter issued within the previous 6 months
explanation: Applicants must obtain, at their own expense, a certified criminal history report from the Georgia Crime Information Center (GCIC), or an equivalent report from their state of residency if not a Georgia resident, that is no more than 60 days old and attached to the application.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, background check requirement

question: Per GREC's Background Clearance Application standards, how does the felony/moral-turpitude ineligibility period for Broker and Associate Broker applicants compare to the general standard?
choice_a: It is identical to the general salesperson standard, with no enhancement for broker applicants
choice_b: It is reduced to 1 year specifically for Broker and Associate Broker applicants
choice_c: It is enhanced to 10 years from the later of conviction, sentencing, or release from incarceration -- beyond the general 2-year (single conviction) or 5-year (multiple convictions) standard
choice_d: It is a permanent, lifetime bar with no possibility of licensure regardless of time elapsed
explanation: While the general standard bars licensure for 2 years after a single felony/moral-turpitude conviction (5 years for multiple such convictions), Broker and Associate Broker applicants face an enhanced bar running 10 years from the later of conviction, sentencing, or release from incarceration.

question: Georgia's mandatory Lawful Presence Affidavit, submitted with every license application, requires the applicant to attest to which minimum age?
choice_c: There is no age attestation on the affidavit
explanation: No standalone numeric age minimum is stated separately in the licensing rules, but the required, notarized Lawful Presence Affidavit that is part of every application has the applicant verify they are '18 years of age or older' -- effectively establishing an 18-year minimum.

question: Which company administers the Georgia real estate broker licensing examination under contract with the Georgia Real Estate Commission (GREC)?
choice_d: GREC administers the exam directly with no third-party vendor
explanation: The current GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin confirms: 'The Georgia Real Estate Commission has contracted with PSI Services LLC (PSI) to conduct the examination testing.'

question: What is the fee to sit for the Georgia broker examination?
explanation: The Salesperson, Broker, and CAM Examination Fee is $175, identical across all three license types, per the current GREC/PSI bulletin.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, fee schedule

question: After passing the broker exam, what is the separate license fee, and how long does the applicant have to apply for the license before the exam results expire?
choice_a: A $170 nonrefundable license fee, with no time limit to apply
choice_b: A $300 refundable license fee, with 90 days to apply
choice_c: A $170 nonrefundable license fee, with one year to apply after passing the exam
choice_d: No separate license fee; the $175 exam fee also covers licensure
explanation: The license fee is a separate, nonrefundable $170, and the applicant has one year after passing the exam to apply for the license before eligibility lapses.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, fee schedule

question: How is the 48-item Georgia Broker Supplement Examination (the state-specific portion of the broker exam) structured?
choice_a: 24 items on State Laws and Rules, 12 items on Management, and 12 items on Closing and Calculations
choice_b: 48 items entirely on State Laws and Rules, with no separate Management or Closing sections
choice_c: 20 items on Management, 20 on Closing and Calculations, and 8 on State Laws and Rules
choice_d: 31 items on State Laws and Rules, 12 items on Management, and 5 items on Closing and Calculations
explanation: The Georgia Broker Supplement Examination totals 48 items, broken out as 31 items on State Laws and Rules (covering topics such as Unfair Practices, Trust Accounts, Substantive Regulations, and Fair Housing Laws), 12 items on Management, and 5 items on Closing and Calculations.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, Georgia Broker Supplement Examination outline

question: Which statement correctly describes Georgia's ongoing education obligations for an already-licensed broker, as compared to a salesperson?
choice_a: Brokers have no separate post-licensing-course requirement (that applies only to salespersons); instead, brokers fall under the standard continuing education renewal cycle of 36 instructional hours per 4-year renewal period, at least 3 of which must be on license-law topics
choice_b: Brokers must complete the same 25-hour post-license course required of salespersons, in addition to the standard CE cycle
choice_c: Brokers are exempt from all continuing education once licensed, unlike salespersons who must renew CE every year
choice_d: Brokers must complete 36 hours of CE every single year, with no 4-year renewal cycle
explanation: The 25-hour post-license course requirement applies only to salespersons under GAC 520-1-.05(1); no distinct broker post-licensing course requirement exists. Instead, brokers renew under the standard cycle requiring 36 instructional hours every 4 years, with at least 3 of those hours specifically on license-law topics.
